Builder result files and scripts were not reused; every number below comes from reviewer scripts in the session scratch folder (blocks.py, sync.cjs, detail.cjs, edge.cjs, browser.cjs, tamper.py). (1) Page diff: f1/index.html has 26 script/style blocks in both versions; only block 16 (MatchLabF1MapComparison) and block 18 (MatchLabF1Comparison) differ; text outside blocks identical; all 9 JSON blocks (dataset, maps, historical, forecasts, tracks, profile-data, f1-history-2024, f1-predictions-2025, f1-query-history) byte-identical; embedded modules equal f1/release-0.26.3/map-comparison.js and comparison.js; the 0.26.2 blocks equal f1/release-0.26.3/map-comparison-0.26.2.js and f1/release-0.8.4/comparison.js; replay module unchanged. No football page changed (only VERSION, package.json, README.md, README.ko.md, CHANGELOG.md bookkeeping). Visible text changes: circuit speed tooltip (recorded GPs) and lane-tab note line, ko/en. (2) Harness on the modules extracted from both pages, 16 recorded 2026 GPs (2024/2025 archive GPs have no laps and no circuit/lane tab; confirmed in Archive.tabs) x 4,001 phases + finish-time neighbourhoods of every predicted rank: predicted P1 lap progress = recorded leader lap progress (max over timeline.state(t)) with max difference 0 in both tabs, and 0 against the reviewer's own raw-lap re-derivation; P1 crosses the line exactly at T (difference 0 s); overtakes 0, backward moves 0, pre-start moves 0, all cars on the line at phase 1; gap rule min(2,(duration-T)/(n-1)) reproduced (13 GPs 2 s, Azerbaijan 1.9595, Bahrain 1.3918, Britain 0.3883); lane and circuit sync objects identical; recorded markers, recorded lanes, unsynced predictedState and timeline identical to 0.26.2 at every sampled phase; 0.26.2 P1 arrived at phase 0.78 in all 16. Upcoming 7 GPs: predicted markers and predictedState identical to 0.26.2 at 2,001 phases, lap count 3, playback 180 s. Other leader definitions: against the position-record P1 the difference is 0 laps at the median in every GP but reaches 1.94 laps (Australia, first 81 s: the position-record leader car 16 has no lap data and sits on the line), 0.84 (Dutch), 0.51 (Canada), 0.30 (Bahrain), always under 2.1% of samples; against a 'most completed laps' leader max 1.0 lap (Canada, around a retirement), otherwise <=0.84. On the circuit canvas the predicted P1 dot vs the recorded position-leader dot is typically 0-1.3% of a lap (median), p90 0-4.3% in 13 GPs; Azerbaijan median 4.6% (systematic GPS vs lap-progress offset); Dutch and Italian GPs p90 31-35% because of red flags (issue R1). Edge cases: safety-car windows (China, Japan, Miami, Monaco, Britain x2, Belgium, Azerbaijan x2, Bahrain): predicted P1 slows exactly with the recorded leader (e.g. China 0.587 laps/90 s vs 0.913 before), P2 and last car slow too. Red flags (Dutch, Italy): lap progress crawls (0.11 / 0.07 laps per 90 s) and predicted cars follow it, but the recorded GPS dots stand still (R1). Leader retirements (Canada car 63, Barcelona car 12, Hungary car 81): no stall, leader curve monotone in all 16 GPs at 0.25 s. Leader identity changes 2-10 per GP without jumps, except a 0.156-lap hop and 11.5 s freeze in Dutch and a 0.054-lap hop in Australia at lap-data gaps (R5). Australia stops at 57/58 in both lane panes (lap 1 not recorded). Visible out-of-sync left for the user: red-flag stretches on the circuit (R1), position-leader vs lap-progress leader differences at a few moments (R2), after the finish the recorded leader dot continues its cool-down lap while predicted cars stop (expected). No blocker. issues.description: Dutch (11353) and Italian (11361) GPs have a 17-20 minute red flag inside one recorded lap. Lap progress crawls linearly through that lap (0.11 / 0.07 laps per 90 s), so predicted cars drive almost a full lap slowly on the circuit while the recorded leader GPS dot stands in the pit lane. Measured: at 60x over 5.8 s the predicted car advanced 0.20 laps on the canvas, the recorded leader 0.0001; the predicted P1 dot is more than 15% of a lap away from the recorded position-leader dot for 21% (Dutch) and 25% (Italy) of the race clock (red flag plus the following SC laps, roughly the first 35-40 min). Lap counts stay equal and the lane tab is unaffected. Not a speed-rule failure but visibly out of sync in 2 of 16 GPs; either explain it on screen or hold predicted cars while the leader is stopped (e.g. use the leader GPS arc / race-control red flag window).

"Follows the leader" means the largest recorded lap progress (the values the recorded side draws). Versus the position-record P1: median 0 laps in all GPs; max 1.94 laps (Australia first 81 s, car 16 has no lap data and is drawn on the line), 0.84 (Dutch, lap-data gap of car 1 around 5,266 s), 0.51 (Canada, retiring leader 63), 0.30 (Bahrain early laps); at most 2.1% of samples above 0.1 lap. On the circuit canvas the predicted P1 dot is typically within 0-1.3% of a lap of the recorded leader dot (median; p90 <= 4.3% in 13 GPs); Azerbaijan shows a systematic ~4.6% offset (GPS position vs lap-progress mapping, 46% of time above 5%).

Lane tab speeds 1x/2x/4x mean the whole race in 60/30/15 s, while circuit 1x is recorded real time. Both lane panes share one phase and measured identical rates (ratio 1.000), so the user request is met inside each tab, but the same label "1x" means different things in the two tabs and the lane tab has no tooltip saying so. Suggest a short ko/en note in the lane tab.

check_release pins the lane module to f1/release-0.26.3/comparison.js and asserts the circuit module calls the shared syncedState, but nothing asserts that the lane draw uses sync. Identical edits to the source and page (restore predictedState in lane draw; change SYNC_GAP_SECONDS) pass once the manifest is regenerated. Same pattern as other repo-pinned modules; code review is the control.

At lap-data gaps the leader curve can hop or pause: Dutch 0.156-lap hop at 5,267.5 s and an 11.5 s freeze (5,191-5,202.5 s) while other cars move; Australia 0.054-lap hop at 81.5 s. All other GPs: max step 0.03 lap per 1.4 s sample, no freeze >= 3 s. After the finish the recorded leader keeps its cool-down lap on GPS while predicted cars stop at the line (Austria, Azerbaijan end offsets) - expected.

SPEC reference column "position-record P1 max" is a sampled value; reviewer sampling gives Canada 0.505 vs SPEC 0.4871 (others match within rounding). Japan 0.26.2 arrival 4,193.5 s rounds to 4,194 in SPEC (reviewer 4,193). All other SPEC numbers reproduce exactly.

issues.description: suspensions() pairs every RED FLAG message with the next restart message. Two RED FLAG messages before one restart (reviewer case: Dutch with a second "RED FLAG - RACE SUSPENDED" 60 s later) create overlapping windows [119.4,1771.5] and [179.4,1771.5]; heldLaps subtracts both overlaps, moving becomes <= 0 and no lap is held, so the whole GP silently falls back to the first-build crawl (R1 returns). Not present in the current 16 GPs (one RED FLAG message each). Fix: merge overlapping windows (or ignore a RED FLAG while a window is open).

A RED FLAG without a later SESSION STARTED / STANDING START / ROLLING START creates no window, so that GP behaves like the first 0.26.3 build (predicted and reconstructed cars crawl through the suspended lap). All current GPs have the restart message. Acceptable fallback; worth a test fixture.

check_release pins call strings (hold=redFlagHold(model,race), const hold=redFlagHold(timeline,race);) but not that recordedState uses the held progress or the ratio value; identical source+page edits (drop progress:hold.progress(d,t), ratio 40) pass once the manifest is regenerated. Same pattern as R4.

Monaco: the winner lap 68 keeps 49.63 s of moving time out of 2,262.7 s, so predicted P1 and reconstructed cars run at 1.547x the median lap pace before and after the suspension (documented by the builder). Dutch/Italy held laps run at 0.555x / 0.549x after the restart. The hold starts at the RED FLAG message time, so in Monaco reconstructed cars stop while GPS cars are still driving to the pit lane. Status text stays "RACING/주행" during the hold (status unchanged by design). R5 hops (Dutch 5,267 s, Australia 81.5 s) are outside held laps and unchanged.
